prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: I can’t name one single “best” broker for everyone — the best choice depends on where you live (Kansas vs Missouri side of Kansas City), what kind of coverage you need (ACA/individual, small‑group, Medicare, Medicaid, dental, etc.), and whether you prefer in‑person help or a digital/phone experience.

How to find the best broker for you
- Decide what type of plan you need (individual/Family ACA plan, employer group, Medicare Part A/B/D/Medigap, Medicaid/CHIP, short‑term).
- Prefer an independent broker or captive agent?
  - Independent broker: represents multiple carriers; usually better for shopping different networks and prices.
  - Captive agent: represents one insurer; may be simpler if you want that carrier.
- Look for experience with your plan type, good reviews, and transparent compensation/disclosures.

Places to search and verify credentials
- NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) “Find an agent” directory.
- State insurance departments: Kansas Insurance Department and Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance — verify licenses and complaints.
- Healthcare.gov “Local help” search for ACA navigators/brokers (for Marketplace plans).
- SHIP/SHICK (State Health Insurance Assistance Programs) for unbiased Medicare counseling.
- Online broker platforms (eHealth, PolicyGenius, etc.) if you prefer quick digital comparisons.

Questions to ask a broker before working with them
- Are you an independent agent or tied to specific carriers?
- Which carriers and plans do you typically work with in Kansas City?
- How many years of experience helping people in my situation?
- Do you help with enrollment, claims, appeals, and renewals? Is there any extra fee?
- How are you compensated? (Most get commissions from carriers; you can ask for disclosure.)
- Can you provide references or local client reviews?

Red flags
- Guarantees of coverage or approval before you apply.
- Pressure to sign immediately or to pick one plan without comparing alternatives.
- Lack of licensing information or unwillingness to disclose carriers they represent.

If you want, I can:
- Find and list several independent brokers or agencies in the Kansas City area (Missouri or Kansas side) — tell me your ZIP code and which type of plan (ACA/individual, Medicare, small group, etc.).
- Or pull up local resources (state DOI links, SHIP contact info) for the exact city/zip.

Which would you like me to do?
